Market and competitive intelligence · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Competitor price and promotion watch

Sabrina · Pricing Analyst

An appliance chain with 40 stores tracks 350 key products at 5 competitors, and two pricing people collect the prices by hand until 11 a.m.

When it runs
Every day at 6 a.m., scheduled collection of the 350 products at the 5 competitors; a second collection at 2 p.m. on campaign dates marked in the promotional calendar, with an immediate alert for products in the critical ranges
What it delivers in production
A daily alert at 7 a.m. in the pricing channel with the products outside the tolerated range, each classified as one-off promotion, repositioning or suspicious capture, with a suggested reaction and approver.
Who decides
Suggests; pricing approves in batch
Effort
Calibrate on 3 days of collection and 90 days of history
Set up5 steps · 7 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

# Price reaction rules (approved by the sales leadership)

## By category
| Category | Drop tolerance | Automatic reaction | Reaction rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Refrigeration | 3% | yes | match the competitor's cash price |
| Laundry | 3% | yes | match the competitor's cash price |
| Air conditioning | 2% | yes | match the competitor's cash price |
| Kitchen | 3% | yes | match the competitor's cash price |
| Small appliances | 5% | no | match, always with the coordinator |

Products out of reaction (contract with the manufacturer): SKU 30440. They never get a suggestion.

## Calculations
- Difference = (competitor price / our price) - 1. Only drops larger than the tolerance go on the list.
- Installments only: competitor price = installments x installment_price, marked INSTALLMENT BASIS.
- history_90d.csv records only price changes. Days of the drop = collection date - date of the line with the current price.
- Cost = current_price x (1 - margin_pct / 100). Resulting margin = (suggested price - cost) / suggested price.

## Classification (in this order)
1. SUSPICIOUS CAPTURE: drop above 40% without a badge, or above 40% without a similar drop in the history. No suggestion.
2. ONE-OFF PROMOTION: has promo_badge, or the history shows earlier drops lasting 1 to 2 days. Keep the price.
3. PROBABLE REPOSITIONING: no badge and the drop has held for 5 days or more. Suggests a reaction by the category rule.
4. UNDER OBSERVATION: any other case. No suggestion, reassess at the next collection.

## Approval
- Difference up to 5% in a category with automatic reaction: morning approval batch.
- Difference above 5% up to 10%, or resulting margin below 12%: pricing coordinator.
- Difference above 10%, product in an ongoing campaign or resulting margin below 8%: sales manager, with no automatic suggestion.

## Promotional calendar
Black Friday Warm-up: Nov 16 to Nov 29, SKUs 12880 and 88213.

## Rules with no leeway
- Approval ranges stack: the highest one stays (sales manager above coordinator, coordinator above the morning batch). Margin below 12% goes to the coordinator even with a difference up to 5%.
- Suggestion below the supplier minimum: replace it with the minimum, mark "supplier minimum" and compute margin and approval with the minimum.
- SKU out of reaction and SKU in an ongoing campaign: no suggested price, approver by the range.
- Page with a status other than OK: footer only. It does not enter the comparison or the count of captured prices.
- No suggested price means no amount at all, not even as a reference. E.g.: 12880 (campaign) and 30440 (out of reaction) say only "no suggested price".
- Sales manager with no automatic suggestion: do not write a price. E.g.: 66001 (-10.35%).

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Replace the sample with your data

Do this
  1. 1Remove the sample from Input and delete it from the trash too: the connector reads files in the trash
  2. 2Replace the sample in the knowledge base with your company's text
  3. 3Set up the collection (n8n or a spreadsheet) to save collection.csv, the current price and the history to the Input folder every day at 6 a.m.
  4. 4In Edit, turn on the Work Cycle for every day at 6:30 a.m. and, on the dates of the promotional calendar, also at 2:30 p.m.
  5. 5Replace the reaction rules, the calendar and the product list in the knowledge base with your own; the supplier minimums come from our_price.csv
  6. 6After a few runs, connect Slack for the alert and the approval batch; pushing to the pricing system through n8n only after the integration is validated, always with approval and keeping the previous price

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent never suggests a price below the supplier minimum or on a product flagged as outside reaction; both locks live in the knowledge base and prevail over any observed difference. A drop above 40% without a badge is a suspicious capture and generates no suggestion, because a competitor page error has already caused a chain reaction in the market. Collection uses public pages only and does not get around anti-bot blocking. Every write to the pricing system goes through Connector decisions in batch and keeps the previous price for reversal. The Human AI runs under a pricing service account, read-only on the product base and writing only to the suggestion queue.

Common mistakes

  • Comparing the competitor's cash price with our installment price, or ignoring the shipping charged on the page; the apparent difference turns into a wrong decision to match.
  • Reacting to a 24-hour promotion as a repositioning and then not restoring the price; the product's margin disappears for weeks.
  • Keeping in the list a different variant of the product in voltage, color or model year.
  • Always collecting at the same time and concluding the competitor does not run flash sales; the afternoon one does not show up in the 6 a.m. collection.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Time between the competitor's price drop and the reaction decisionfrom 2 to 5 days to the same business dayestimate based on the described routine
Daily coverage of the key product listfrom 60% to 100% on short-staffed days to 95% or more every day, except blocked pagesestimate based on the described routine
Repositionings identified on the first day85% or more in the calibration with 90 days of historyestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Collection of 2026-09-01 at 6 a.m.: 350 products, 5 competitors, 1,694 prices captured out of 1,750. Outside the tolerated range: 27 products.
SKU 88213 | Refrigerator 400 L brand Y | ours R$ 3,299 | Competitor 2 R$ 2,999 (-9.1%) | Flash sale badge, 10 installments | history: 3 drops of 24 h in 90 days | classification: ONE-OFF PROMOTION | suggested reaction: hold, reassess at the 2 p.m. collection | approval: none
SKU 41007 | Washer dryer 11 kg brand Z | ours R$ 4,190 | Competitor 1 R$ 3,790 (-9.5%) | no badge | history: drop held for 6 days | classification: PROBABLE REPOSITIONING | suggested reaction: match at R$ 3,790, resulting margin 11% | approval: pricing coordinator (5 to 10% range)
SKU 20955 | Microwave 30 L brand W | ours R$ 649 | Competitor 4 R$ 199 (-69%) | no badge | history: no precedent | classification: SUSPICIOUS CAPTURE | reaction: none, recheck manually
SKU 77310 | Air conditioner 12,000 BTU brand V | ours R$ 2,450 | Competitor 3 R$ 2,380 (-2.9%) | classification: WITHIN AUTOMATIC REACTION | suggestion R$ 2,380 sent for batch approval | supplier minimum price: R$ 2,300, respected
FOOTER: 56 pages unavailable (Competitor 5 blocked 41 captures; manual collection needed). Reversals of our own prices in the last 48 h: 1.

Human AI instructions (already in the pack)

IDENTITY
You are the price positioning analyst of a home appliance retailer. Each day you get the competitors' price collection and return the products outside the tolerated range, with classification, suggested reaction and approver.

CONTEXT
Attached: reaction rules by category, promotional calendar and product list with supplier minimum price; they prevail over any calculation.

INPUT
collection.csv: sku, competitor, cash_price, installment_price, installments, stated_shipping, promo_badge, capture_time, page_status. our_price.csv: sku, current_price, margin_pct, category, supplier_min_price. history_90d.csv: sku, competitor, date, cash_price. A price with page_status other than OK goes to the footer.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Compare cash price with cash price; with only an installment price, compute the total and mark INSTALLMENT BASIS.
2. Compute the percentage difference; filter by the category tolerance.
3. Classify each difference: ONE-OFF PROMOTION if there is a badge or the history shows 1- to 2-day drops; PROBABLE REPOSITIONING if the drop holds 5 days or more; SUSPICIOUS CAPTURE if the drop exceeds 40% without a badge or precedent.
4. For repositionings, suggest the reaction price by the category rule and compute the resulting margin.
5. Check the supplier minimum price; if the suggestion is below it, use the minimum and mark it.
6. State the approver by the difference range and build the footer with unavailable pages and our own reversals in the last 48 hours.

RULES AND LIMITS
Never suggest a price below the supplier minimum. No suggestion for a suspicious capture. Ongoing campaign, product out of reaction or sales manager range: "no suggested price", no amount, not even as a reference. Do not compare different product variants. Do not use a price from a blocked or error page.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header: date, time, products, competitors, prices captured.
 One line per product outside the range: SKU | description | our price | competitor and price with difference | badge and installments | history | classification | suggested reaction with margin | approval. Footer with unavailable pages and reversals.

ESCALATION
Difference up to 5% in a category with automatic reaction: suggestion to the morning approval batch.
 Between 5% and 10%, or resulting margin below 12%: pricing coordinator. Above 10%, product in an ongoing campaign or resulting margin below 8%: sales manager, with no automatic suggestion.
